_meta.population: English course, 9,031 rows with an English definition
questions: does the English definition give the sense a learner meets
does the Arabic render THAT sense with matching part of speech
_meta.contract: translate.maker_system: 'the single word or short phrase a native speaker would use for THAT specific sense ... Match the part of speech.'
_meta.judge: in-session Claude panel; NOT human review

en_definition: belonging to you
note: Only sense of the determiner. The Arabic gives the 2nd-person singular possessive suffixes (m/f) correctly, though it omits dual/plural (ـكما / ـكم / ـكن) — an incompleteness, not a divergence.

en_definition: people or things already mentioned, as the subject ('___ are here')
note: Good card. One support-locale precision point: هم is masculine plural only; Arabic also needs هنّ (fem. pl.) and هما (dual), so the gloss under-specifies for an Arabic-speaking learner. Faithful to the English as given.

en_definition: in the company of; also names the tool used ('cut it ___ a knife')
note: Both stated uses are the core ones, and the example sentence earns its place. Arabic مَعَ covers only the accompaniment half; instrumental 'with' in Arabic is the prefix بـ, so the gloss is incomplete for the second clause rather than contradictory — worth a second Arabic gloss here.

en_definition: therefore; to such a degree
note: Both senses given are the everyday ones, and pairing them is sensible for a function word. Arabic لِذَا; جِدًّا maps one-to-one onto 'therefore; to such a degree'.

en_definition: used of a single unit or thing; not two or more
note: Correct adjective sense. Arabic واحد matches.

en_definition: marks the future; also a promise
note: Correct and well pitched for the auxiliary at rank 57. Arabic سوف / سـ are exactly the future markers; the 'also a promise' half is not rendered, but nothing in the Arabic contradicts the definition.

en_definition: give information to a particular person; it needs a hearer ('___ me the truth')
note: Core sense of the verb, and the usage note about needing a hearer is genuinely the distinguishing feature against 'say'. أخبر matches.

en_definition: asks which person ('___ is that?')
note: The interrogative is the sense a beginner meets first, so primary is right, but the relative-pronoun use ("the man who came") is at least as frequent at rank 64 and is uncovered. Arabic مين is colloquial (Egyptian/Levantine); MSA is مَنْ. It conveys the right meaning, so not a divergence, but it is a register defect on a support-locale card and it is a bare gloss rather than a rendering of "asks which person".

en_definition: belonging to him
note: Plain and correct. Arabic gives the possessive suffix ـهُ, the right functional equivalent for a determiner.

en_definition: must have something, because you cannot manage without it ('I ___ help')
note: Good learner-style definition with an example frame; primary sense. اِحْتَاجَ is the correct verb citation form and matches the part of speech.

en_definition: any object or matter you do not name exactly ('what's that ___?')
note: Well-built high-frequency card with a usage example. The Arabic شي is the colloquial spelling; MSA is شيء with the hamza. Meaning is right — flag for the orthography pass, not the sense pass.

en_definition: belonging to us
note: Correct. ـنا is the right rendering given Arabic has no free-standing possessive determiner.

en_definition: used to form the comparative of some adjectives and adverbs
note: Borderline call. For the adverb the periphrastic-comparative use ('more difficult') is genuinely the commonest thing a learner meets, so the sense is right — but the definition is metalinguistic, describing a grammatical function rather than stating a meaning, so it is near-useless as a recognition prompt. It would read far better as 'to a greater degree or extent'. Flagging as a phrasing defect rather than a sense defect, hence primary. Arabic أكثر is the right gloss.

en_definition: phone or shout to someone; also give a name to ('they ___ him Bob')
note: Reads as a hand-written multi-sense card rather than a database gloss, and it works: phoning and naming are the two dominant uses at rank 99. Arabic دَعَا covers summoning and naming (دعاه بوب) but not telephoning, which is اتَّصَل — and phoning is the sense the English definition puts first, so the single-word gloss drops the heaviest part.

en_definition: (plural) any group of human beings (men or women or children) collectively
note: English is correct and unremarkable. The Arabic خَلْق means 'creation / created beings' — a literary usage that can mean 'people' but adds a created-by-God framing the definition does not have, and it is not the word a beginner needs at rank 104. النَّاس (or أَشْخَاص for countable individuals) is the gloss this card should carry.

en_definition: feeling or expressing regret or sorrow or a sense of loss over something done or undone
note: English is the correct commonest sense (the apology/regret one). The Arabic is the wrong voice: مُؤْسِف means 'regrettable, causing sorrow' — it describes the thing one is sorry about, not the person feeling regret. The definition says 'feeling or expressing regret', which is آسِف. مُؤْسِف would fit a different sense of 'sorry' ('a sorry state'), so a learner at rank 113 gets the apology word glossed as the wrong participle. High-value fix: this is a top-500 word.

en_definition: at all, even slightly (in questions and negative statements)
note: The definition is right for the adverb POS given ('is it any better?'), even though most of the rank-116 frequency is the determiner. The Arabic أَيّ is the determiner gloss and does not convey 'at all, even slightly' — expected على الإطلاق (or بأي قدر) for the adverbial sense.

en_definition: (quantifier used with mass nouns) great in quantity or degree or extent
note: Correct quantifier sense with the mass-noun restriction usefully stated. كثير matches.

en_definition: a period of time containing 365 (or 366) days
note: Correct and plain. Arabic سنة matches.

en_definition: inquire about
note: Commonest sense, though 'inquire about' is terse for a rank-135 word. سأل is exact.

en_definition: a thing of any kind, in questions and negatives ('did you see ___?')
note: Good card — the usage note about questions and negatives is exactly what a learner needs. أَيُّ شَيْءٍ matches; it drops the usage note but says nothing the English does not.

en_definition: put into service; make work or employ for a particular purpose or for its inherent or natural purpose
note: Primary sense, but the WordNet phrasing is heavy for a rank-144 word — "for its inherent or natural purpose" adds nothing a beginner can act on. Arabic اِسْتِعْمَال is a verbal noun ("usage"), while the headword and definition are verbal; it should be اِسْتَعْمَلَ or يَسْتَخْدِم. Note the inconsistency with "need", where the verb form was used correctly — worth checking whether verb entries across the deck are systematically glossed as masdars.

en_definition: it is necessary to
note: Exactly the sense of this very high-frequency modal, and short enough to read at a glance. Arabic وَجَبَ is past tense where the English is present ('it is necessary to'); يَجِب would match the definition's tense. Minor, but on a rank-150 card worth getting right.

en_definition: a person you know well and regard with affection and trust
note: English is exactly right. The Arabic is the weak link: صاحب reads first as 'owner of / possessor' in MSA and only carries 'friend' colloquially, while صديق is the standard equivalent and the one that matches 'a person you know well and regard with affection and trust'. This is a translation defect, not a consequence of the English choice.

en_definition: an adult female person (as opposed to a man)
note: Commonest sense, plainly stated. Arabic اِمْرَأَة matches.

en_definition: (often followed by `of') a large number or amount or extent
note: Correct sense for 'a lot of'. The bare-backtick parenthetical '(often followed by `of')' is raw database formatting and should be cleaned up on the card. كثير is right.

en_definition: a male parent; also a way of addressing one's own male parent
note: English is correct for rank 183. Arabic بابا is the informal vocative 'dad/papa' — it renders only the second half of the definition ('a way of addressing one's own male parent') and not the headline 'a male parent', which is أب. Expected Arabic: أب (optionally أب / بابا to keep both halves).

en_definition: a youthful male person
note: Clean card.

en_definition: a group of things that are the same in some way; also 'gentle and caring' ('a ___ person')
note: Good card: the noun sense first and the adjective sense flagged with a cloze example, which is the right treatment for a word this frequent with two unrelated senses. The Arabic renders only the first half (نوع = type); the 'gentle and caring' half is dropped entirely, so an Arabic-reading learner loses the sense they are arguably likelier to need. Suggest نوع، صنف؛ وأيضاً: لطيف، عطوف.

en_definition: pleasant and agreeable — of a day, a meal or a place as well as a person ('what a ___ day')
note: English side is exactly right, including the reminder that it applies to days and meals, not just people. The Arabic is broken: حَسَّن (with shadda) is the form II VERB 'to improve, to make better', not an adjective at all. The intended word is probably حَسَن ('good'), but for this definition لطيف or جميل is what a learner needs. Wrong part of speech and wrong meaning on a rank-197 card.

en_definition: the present time or age
expected: this day; the day that is happening now
note: 'The present time or age' is the 'youth of today' sense. At rank 218 the learner means 'this day'. The Arabic اليوم is the day-sense (it can stretch to 'nowadays', so the divergence is arguable — flagged at low confidence), which means the Arabic is right and the English is the one that missed.

en_definition: the upper part of the human body or the front part of the body in animals; contains the face and brains
note: Body-part sense, exactly right for rank 224. Arabic راس is spelled without the hamza; the standard orthography is رَأْس. Cosmetic, not a meaning problem.

en_definition: slang for sexual intercourse
expected: a very rude swear word used to express anger or surprise, or for emphasis; also vulgar slang for sex
note: The intercourse sense is genuine but is not why this word sits at rank 258 — that is the expletive/intensifier ('what the fuck', 'give a fuck', 'fuck off'). Even restricted to pos=noun, the frequent noun use is 'not give a fuck'. Arabic نيك is the correct vulgar noun for intercourse, i.e. a faithful rendering of the definition as given.

en_definition: be seated
note: 'be seated' is terse but unambiguous at rank 259. قعد is the ordinary colloquial-standard equivalent.

en_definition: cause to go somewhere
note: Broad but correct for the commonest sense; أرسل is exact.

en_definition: a unit of language that native speakers can identify
note: Right sense. 'A unit of language that native speakers can identify' is a linguist's formulation of it; the sense is correct but the phrasing is above the level of a rank-284 card. كلمة is exact.

en_definition: the organ of sight
note: Commonest sense, plainly worded. عين matches.

en_definition: a shelter serving as a place of safety or sanctuary
note: 'Place of safety or sanctuary' is exactly what an ordinary speaker means (safe haven). ملاذ = refuge/sanctuary, matches.

en_definition: a drawn-out sound of relief or pleasure ('___, that's better')
expected: a sound you make when you suddenly understand or notice something, or feel relief
note: Relief/pleasure is a genuine use, but the commonest 'ah' in the dialogue a learner meets at rank 306 is realisation ('ah, I see'). The Arabic آه is chiefly a sigh of pain, grief or longing — close to the opposite of 'relief or pleasure' — so the support line misdirects here; آه is not a safe one-word equivalent for this interjection.

en_definition: refers back to the speaker ('I told ___')
note: Correct and the cloze example disambiguates it from 'me'. نفسي is exact.

en_definition: hesitation sound while thinking; spelled u-m, not u-h
note: Correct sense. The trailing 'spelled u-m, not u-h' is authoring metadata disambiguating it from 'uh' — it reads oddly on a learner-facing card and should be dropped or moved out of the definition line. Arabic إمم supplies the equivalent hesitation sound rather than translating 'hesitation sound while thinking'; useful for the learner, but it conveys no explanation.

en_definition: expect and wish
note: English sense is right, though 'expect and wish' overstates the expectation — hoping is wanting under uncertainty. The Arabic is the defect: أَمَل vocalised that way is the NOUN 'hope', not a verb, while the card's POS is verb. Expected يَأْمَل (or يَتَمَنَّى / يَرْجُو).

en_definition: a polite name for any woman
note: Correct and appropriately plain for a top-500 word. Arabic سَيِّدَة matches.

en_definition: a defense of some offensive behavior or some failure to keep a promise etc.
note: The noun sense given is the right one for a noun entry, though at rank 327 the word is met overwhelmingly in the verb formula 'excuse me', which this card does not cover. The Arabic عَذَرَ is the perfect-tense VERB 'he pardoned/excused' — a different word class and a different referent from 'a defense of some offensive behavior'. The noun is عُذْر.

en_definition: something determined in relation to something that includes it
note: Correct commonest sense (a piece of a whole), but the phrasing 'something determined in relation to something that includes it' is near-opaque for a rank-336 card; 'a piece or section of something larger' would carry the same sense. Arabic جزء matches the sense.

en_definition: a geometric element that has position but no extension
expected: the main idea or purpose of something; also a particular place, moment, or score
note: Euclidean geometry sense ('position but no extension') displacing the everyday senses at rank 343 — a learner meets 'that's not the point', 'at this point', 'scored a point'. Arabic نقطة is a headword gloss that does cover the geometric point, so it is not a mistranslation, but it renders none of the definition's technical restriction.

en_definition: cause to move by striking
expected: to strike someone or something with your hand or an object
note: 'Cause to move by striking' is the hit-a-ball sense — real and common in sport, but it is not what 'he hit me' means, and at rank 347 the plain striking sense is what the learner needs. A clear case of the database's sense order not matching frequency. The Arabic ضرب drops the 'cause to move' element and gives the general striking sense, which happens to be closer to the right sense than the English is; marking faithful since it does not contradict the definition.

en_definition: the tangible substance that goes into the makeup of a physical object
expected: things in general; belongings or unspecified items ('put your ___ over there')
note: The material/substance sense is real ('what's this stuff made of?', 'the stuff of dreams') but at rank 356 the learner meets 'stuff' as 'things/belongings' almost every time. Notably the Arabic أشياء ('things') gives the CORRECT everyday sense and therefore does not translate the definition shown — the two sides disagree, with the Arabic being the better of the pair.

en_definition: within a building
note: English is fine — 'within a building' is the main adverbial sense ('come inside'), if slightly narrow. The Arabic is the defect: في بَطْن means 'in the belly/interior of' and is neither a rendering of 'within a building' nor a usable gloss of the adverb. Expected في الداخل or داخل المبنى.

en_definition: a rational motive for a belief or action
note: The 'why' sense, which is what a learner meets at rank 395. 'Rational motive' is a little formal but lands on the right concept. سبب is exact.

en_definition: a person of no influence
expected: no person; not anyone
note: 'A nobody' = an unimportant person is genuine, but rank 419 is driven by the pronoun use ('nobody came'), which this card never shows. WordNet has no pronoun POS, which is likely how the noun sense got tagged here. Arabic شخص تافه is a shade harsher than 'of no influence' (تافه = worthless/trivial); شخص لا أهمية له would sit closer.

en_definition: go across or through
expected: to move past or go by; also to hand something to someone
note: 'Go across or through' is genuine (pass through a tunnel) but is not what a learner meets first at rank 428 — that is 'go past / move by' and 'hand over'. This is WordNet sense-1 ordering rather than frequency ordering. Arabic يمر faithfully renders the definition as written.

en_definition: sound loudly and sonorously
note: The bell/phone-sound sense is the right verb sense, but 'sound loudly and sonorously' fits a church bell and not a mobile phone, which is where a learner actually meets it; 'to make the sound of a bell, or (of a phone) to sound to signal a call' would be plainer. The Arabic is the real defect: خاتم is the NOUN 'finger ring', so the card pairs a verb definition with a noun translation in a different sense. It is also the only Arabic entry in the batch without diacritics.

en_definition: bring something to an end; reach the end of something
note: Correct core sense for rank 438. The Arabic فَرَغَ ('be done with, be free of', and unvocalised also 'be empty') is a weak choice for a transitive 'bring something to an end'; أَنْهَى / أَتَمَّ is the direct equivalent, or انْتَهَى مِن for the intransitive.

en_definition: place of business where professional or clerical duties are performed
note: Commonest sense; مَكْتَب is the standard equivalent (also covers 'desk', harmless here).

en_definition: a perceptible indication of something not immediately apparent (as a visible clue that something has happened)
expected: a board or notice with words or a picture on it, giving information or a warning; also something that shows that something exists or may happen
note: The 'indication/clue' sense is real and frequent, but at rank 448 the first thing an ordinary speaker means by 'sign' is the physical notice — road sign, shop sign, stop sign. A learner recognising the card from this gloss would still miss the concrete use they meet daily. إِشَارَة faithfully renders the indication/signal gloss as written.

en_definition: fasten something at the top so it dangles; dangle from a support above
note: Core literal sense, correctly chosen over the execution sense. عَلَّق matches. (At this rank much of the usage is phrasal — hang on, hang out, hang up — but the literal sense is the right base for the card.)

en_definition: let fall to the ground
note: Commonest sense at this rank, plainly worded. Arabic أسقط matches the causative English.

en_definition: lacking or marked by lack of intellectual acuity
note: Right sense, wordy phrasing ('intellectual acuity' is above the level of a rank-475 card). غَبِيّ matches.

en_definition: let out a long, deep breath, showing tiredness, relief, or sadness
note: Everyday sense, and the definition even names the feelings that prompt it. تَنَهَّدَ is exact.

en_definition: amounting to one more than five; 6
note: Numeral sense; unambiguous. سِتَّة is the standard citation form.

en_definition: a person who exercises control over workers
note: Correct commonest sense. Arabic رَئِيس is broad (chief/president) where مُدِير would be tighter for a workplace boss, but it is not a different sense.

en_definition: an institution created to conduct business
note: Business-firm sense is clearly first; 'companionship' and the military unit are secondary. شَرِكَة is exact.

en_definition: informal terms for a mother
note: Right sense. Two wording issues: the plural 'informal terms for a mother' is a lexical-database artefact (should be 'an informal word for mother'), and rank 531 is suspiciously high for this word — it likely absorbs the unrelated abbreviations MA (Master of Arts, Massachusetts, milliamp), which is a ranking problem upstream of the definition. ماما matches the informal register well.

en_definition: write down or store information; also (noun) a written account of past events, or a disc of music
note: Good learner definition — the verb sense first, with the two common noun senses appended. The Arabic أُسْطُوَانَة translates only the final fragment ('a disc of music') and leaves the verb sense and the 'written account' sense untranslated. An Arabic-speaking learner reads this card as 'vinyl record' only.

en_definition: touch with the lips or press the lips (against someone's mouth or other body part) as an expression of love, greeting, etc.
note: Full, ordinary sense. Arabic باس is correct but colloquial/dialectal; MSA قبّل would match the register of the rest of the batch.

en_definition: unique or specific to a person or thing or category
expected: better or different from what is usual; exceptional
note: 'Unique or specific to a person or thing or category' is the 'particular' sense (special case, special purpose), genuinely common, but at rank 542 the sense met first is 'not ordinary, exceptional' ('a special day', 'you're special'). Arabic خاص translates the definition's specific/particular sense accurately.

en_definition: start using violence against a person, place, or group
note: Commonest sense, and it avoided the medical 'a heart attack' and sporting senses. هَاجَمَ matches.

en_definition: destroy by fire
note: 'Destroy by fire' is a fair core sense, though it is transitive-only and the intransitive 'be on fire, produce flames' is at least as common at this rank. The Arabic is the real problem: احترق is the intransitive 'to burn / be consumed by fire', while the English definition is causative ('destroy by fire') — that is أحرق. The Arabic card therefore teaches the opposite valency from the English one.

en_definition: capable of happening or existing
note: Core sense. ممكن matches.

en_definition: being one more than nine
note: Correct, if phrased as a riddle ('being one more than nine'); 'the number 10' would be kinder on a card. عَشَرَة matches.

en_definition: shield from danger, injury, destruction, or damage
note: Clean, recognisable definition of the core sense. حَمَى matches.

en_definition: a person who lacks good judgment
note: Right sense. Arabic مُغَفَّل leans to 'gullible dupe' where the English says 'lacks good judgment' (أَحْمَق is the closer match) — a nuance shift, not a different sense.

en_definition: restore by replacing a part or putting together what is torn or broken
note: Repair sense, correct. يصلح matches.

en_definition: make a sound that shows delight or admiration
note: The meaning is right. In practice it is an interjection ('Ooh, nice!') rather than the verb the card tags, though the verb use ('oohing and aahing') is genuine; the sense transfers either way. Arabic يتعجب shifts it twice: to astonishment rather than delight or admiration, and it loses the 'make a sound' element entirely. It is a defensible one-word gloss with no neat alternative, so mark this low-confidence divergence rather than a clear error.

en_definition: roused to anger; - Mark Twain
note: 'Roused to anger' is the commonest sense in US English; in British English 'insane' leads, so this is a defensible primary rather than a clean one. Carries the same '; - Mark Twain' citation artifact as 'nicer'. The Arabic مَجْنُون means insane — it translates the sense the English did NOT choose; angry would be غاضب. Either the English or the Arabic has to move.

en_definition: discover or determine the existence, presence, or fact of
note: Standard everyday verb sense: become aware of, perceive. لاحظ is the exact equivalent and matches the definition's sense.

en_definition: a facility equipped with special equipment and personnel for a particular purpose
expected: a place where trains or buses stop for passengers; also a building for a public service (police, fire) or a radio or TV channel
note: Not wrong, but abstract to the point of being unrecognisable: 'a facility equipped with special equipment and personnel for a particular purpose' would not let a learner guess 'station', and at rank 684 the train/bus sense is the anchor. Arabic مَحَطَّة tracks the definition acceptably, though note it covers transit, broadcast and power stations but NOT a police station (مركز شرطة) — so the Arabic is narrower than the generic English gloss.

en_definition: a detailed critical inspection
expected: the activity of learning about a subject; also a piece of research on something
note: "A detailed critical inspection" is the examination sense; at rank 693 a learner meets "study" as learning (her studies) or as a research report (a study found). Separately, the Arabic تَعَلُّم means 'learning', which is not what the English definition says — so this card is defective twice over, in different places.

en_definition: a public official who decides cases in a court; also (verb) to decide the result of a contest
expected: to form an opinion about someone or something; to decide a case in court
note: Card is tagged verb but the definition leads with the noun (public official), and the verb sense it does give — deciding a contest — is not the commonest verb use. Arabic حَكَمَ is a correct verb rendering and matches the POS, though it leaves the noun half of the English untranslated.

en_definition: any number of entities (members) considered as a unit
note: Right sense, dictionary register ('entities (members) considered as a unit'). 'A number of people or things together' would read better, but the sense selection is correct.

en_definition: consider or hold as true
expected: to agree to take or receive something offered
note: 'Consider or hold as true' is the 'accept a theory' sense; at rank 711 the learner meets accepting a gift, an invitation, a job. Arabic قَبِلَ is the general verb and covers the definition's sense as well as the commoner one, so it is not itself wrong — though a strict rendering of 'hold as true' would be سلّم بـ.

en_definition: primarily temporal sense; indicating or being or seeming to be limited in duration
expected: small in length or height; not long or tall
note: The temporal sense displaces the spatial one that everybody thinks of first at rank 714. Worse, the WordNet metalinguistic tag 'primarily temporal sense;' has leaked onto the card and reads as gibberish to a learner — strip that whatever sense you keep. Arabic قصير covers both length and duration, so it does not contradict the gloss.

en_definition: your basis for belief or disbelief; knowledge on which to base belief
note: Correct sense but framed epistemologically ('your basis for belief or disbelief') rather than in the way the word is actually used — facts or information that show something is true, especially in court. A plainer card would read 'facts or information that show something is true'. Arabic دَلِيل covers proof/indication and matches.

en_definition: move upward
note: English 'move upward' is the right general sense (smoke rises, the sun rises, prices rise). Arabic نَهَضَ is narrower and different: it means to get to one's feet from sitting or lying. The definition as given calls for اِرْتَفَعَ (or صَعِدَ). A learner would map 'rise' onto standing up only.

en_definition: an unfortunate person who suffers from some adverse circumstance
note: Right sense; the gloss is a little abstract ('adverse circumstance') but recognisable. ضَحِيَّة is exact.

en_definition: prepare a hot meal
note: Acceptable, though 'prepare a hot meal' is narrower than use — it misses the transitive 'cook the rice / cook the chicken' pattern a learner meets constantly. Arabic طبخ is exact.

en_definition: a permanent organization of the military land forces of a nation or state
note: Correct commonest sense, if stiffly worded. جَيْش is a headword gloss rather than a rendering of the definition, but it names the same thing.

en_definition: draw air into, and expel out of, the lungs
note: Plain, recognisable, correct. تَنَفَّسَ matches exactly.

en_definition: travel across or pass over
note: Primary verb sense. Arabic عبر matches exactly.

en_definition: taking a vaccine as a precaution against contracting a disease
note: Correct everyday sense. Minor wording quibble: it frames the act from the recipient's side ('taking a vaccine'), where 'the giving or receiving of a vaccine' would cover both. تطعيم is the standard term.

en_definition: free from favoritism or self-interest or bias or deception; conforming with established standards or rules
note: The just/impartial sense is the right one for the adjective. The wording bolts on a second sense ('conforming with established standards or rules') and would read better trimmed to the first clause. Arabic حقّاني does mean just/equitable and is faithful, but it is a high-register, slightly unusual choice; عادل or مُنصِف is the natural word.

en_definition: the place where some action occurs
expected: a part of a film, play, or book showing one piece of action in one place
note: 'The place where some action occurs' is the scene-of-the-crime sense — real and common, but the first sense for most speakers is the film/play section. Separately, the Arabic is a genuine translation defect: مَنْظَر means 'a view, a sight', which is a third sense and not what the English definition says. The definition as given would be مَسْرَح الحَدَث or مَوْقِع; the film sense would be مَشْهَد.

en_definition: any mechanical or electrical device that transmits or modifies energy to perform or assist in the performance of human tasks
note: Correct core sense. Very long for a card — 'a device with moving parts that does work, powered by electricity or an engine' would be recognisable faster. Arabic آلَة matches.

en_definition: a division of an ocean or a large body of salt water partially enclosed by land
note: Standard definition. The Arabic gloss is vocalised wrongly: it should be بَحْر (sukun on the ḥāʾ), not بَحَر. Consonantal text and meaning are right, so this is a diacritics defect for the vowelling pass, not a sense divergence.

en_definition: stay in the same state or condition; continue to be
note: Commonest sense ('remain calm', 'remains true'). بَقِيَ matches.

en_definition: the organization that is the governing authority of a political unit
note: Standard sense, standard translation.

en_definition: a proposition deducible from basic postulates
note: Only sense of the word, so the sense choice is right, but the wording ("deducible from basic postulates") is opaque for a card — "a statement in mathematics that has been proved to be true" would be recognisable. Two data bugs worth chasing: pos is tagged "propn" when theorem is a common noun, and rank 847 is implausible for general English, which suggests a maths-heavy source corpus. Arabic نظرية is the usual term in maths (نظرية فيثاغورس) but is ambiguous with "theory"; مبرهنة is unambiguous.

en_definition: a professional person authorized to practice law; conducts lawsuits or gives legal advice
note: Textbook primary sense; محامٍ is the exact equivalent.

en_definition: the person you are married to, or live with as a couple
note: Defensible as primary — bare "my partner" in speech means spouse/significant other, and learner dictionaries lead with it — but the business/collaborator sense is a close rival at this rank and the card covers only one. Arabic شريك on its own reads as business partner or associate and does not convey "married to or living with as a couple"; that sense needs شريك الحياة or a gloss.

en_definition: the study and classification of human societies
note: Correct sense; 'and classification' is harmless padding. Separately, rank 853 for 'sociology' looks implausible for a general-frequency list — worth checking the rank source, not the definition.

en_definition: increase the likelihood of
expected: ask someone to come to an event or place
note: Clear displacement: 'increase the likelihood of' is the figurative use in 'invite trouble / invite criticism' — real and reasonably common in writing, but not remotely what a learner meets at rank 854. Arabic دَعَا is the everyday 'invited/called' sense and does not translate 'increase the likelihood of' at all, so English and Arabic are describing two different senses on one card. Fixing the English resolves both.

en_definition: one of the groups of Christians who have their own beliefs and forms of worship
expected: a building where Christians meet to worship
note: This is the denomination sense (the Methodist Church, the Orthodox Church) — real and common, but not what most people mean first. At rank 881 the learner meets the building and the service ('go to church'). Arabic كنيسة spans building and institution just as English does, so it does not misstate the definition; the defect is the English sense choice.

en_definition: feeling or showing anger
note: Only real sense. غاضب matches.

en_definition: a point located with respect to surface features of some region
note: The 'place' sense is correct and arguably the commonest, but the wording is a topographic-gazetteer gloss — 'a point located with respect to surface features of some region' is unreadable at rank 898; 'a particular place' does the job. Note the small-mark/stain sense is nearly as frequent and is not covered. بُقْعَة carries both place and stain, so it is compatible but vague; مَكَان would pin the given sense.

en_definition: put an end to a state or an activity
note: English sense is the everyday one (quit smoking, quit a job). The Arabic تخلى عن means 'abandon / relinquish / forsake' — it takes something you renounce rather than an activity you stop, and is not idiomatic for the definition as given. توقف عن / أقلع عن (stop doing) or استقال من (leave a job) would render it.

en_definition: someone who causes the death of a person or animal
note: Commonest everyday sense. قاتل is the direct equivalent.

en_definition: imagine to be the case or true or probable
note: 'I suspect he's right' is common and this covers it. What is missing is the other everyday sense — believing someone guilty of a crime — which at this rank a learner meets constantly in dialogue; a card reading 'think something is probably true, especially something bad' would carry both. Arabic يظن ('thinks, supposes') translates the definition as given, and inherits the same gap.

en_definition: call upon in supplication; entreat
note: English sense is right (plead/entreat) though the register is formal — 'ask someone earnestly for something' would read better. The Arabic بيك is not a word for 'beg' at all: it reads as the title 'Bey' or Egyptian colloquial 'in/with you', and looks like a transliteration artefact of the English headword. Correct would be توسّل / استجدى / رجا. This is a pure translation defect on an otherwise sound card.

en_definition: a mountain or tall hill
expected: Ben — a man's name, short for Benjamin
note: "A mountain or tall hill" is the Scottish usage (Ben Nevis) — genuine but regional and not something a learner will use. Rank 927 almost certainly comes from the personal name Ben in the corpus, not from the Scottish noun; this entry probably should not be a card at all. Arabic بَان does not mean mountain or hill (that is جبل / تل) — it reads as the ben/moringa tree or the verb 'became clear'.

en_definition: not disposed to cheat or defraud; not deceptive or fraudulent
note: Commonest sense. نزيه ('of integrity, incorruptible') tracks 'not disposed to cheat or defraud' well; صادق/أمين would be the alternatives.

en_definition: an event that happens
note: Correct everyday sense. Mildly tautological ('an event that happens') but recognisable. Arabic حدث matches.

en_definition: a set of rooms on one floor of a building, used as a home
note: Clean, concrete, exactly the sense at this rank. Arabic شقة is exact.

en_definition: feeling hunger; feeling a need or desire to eat food
note: Core sense, and the second clause makes it recognisable without circularity. جَائِع matches.

en_definition: a committee having supervisory powers
expected: a long flat piece of wood or other stiff material
note: Clearest miss in the batch, and the Arabic proves it. 'A committee having supervisory powers' is the board-of-directors sense — real, but not what an ordinary speaker reaches for first at rank 968 (plank, notice board, blackboard, chopping board). Note the Arabic disagrees with its own English: لَوْحَة is a flat panel/plank/sign-board, never a committee — that would be مجلس (إدارة). So this card shows one sense in English and a different one in Arabic, which is the worst case for a learner.

en_definition: not capable of occurring or being accomplished or dealt with
note: Correct. Arabic مُسْتَحِيل matches.

en_definition: morally bad or wrong
note: Commonest sense, short and recognisable. Form mismatch on the Arabic: شَرّ is the noun 'evil'; for pos=adj the match is شِرِّير.

en_definition: (computer science) the code that identifies where a piece of information is stored
expected: the details of where someone lives or where mail is sent
note: Computer-science memory-address sense displacing the postal sense a learner actually meets ('what's your address?'). Arabic عنوان covers both the postal and the computing sense, so it is a fair gloss of the headword, but it does not render the '(computer science)' restriction — the Arabic learner reads the postal sense the English denies them.

en_definition: a lump or mass of hard consolidated mineral matter
note: Commonest sense. حجر matches.

en_definition: utter a sudden loud cry
note: Commonest sense. صَاحَ ('shout, cry out') matches well.

en_definition: having or producing a comfortable and agreeable degree of heat or imparting or maintaining heat
note: Right sense; the 'or imparting or maintaining heat' tail is redundant but harmless. دَافِئ matches.

en_definition: buildings for carrying on industrial labor
expected: a living thing that grows in the ground — a tree, flower, grass or vegetable
note: The factory sense is real and common, but at rank 1089 a learner meets 'plant' as vegetation first. The Arabic نَبَات is the botanical sense, so the card's two halves contradict each other: an Arabic speaker reads 'plant = vegetation' while the English defines a factory. Clearest defect in the batch.

en_definition: engage in sexual intercourse
expected: (of animals) to come together to produce young; to breed
note: The verb 'mate' is met almost entirely in the animal-breeding sense; 'engage in sexual intercourse' is the human-centred WordNet gloss shared with copulate/pair/couple, and a learner would not recover 'mate' from it. Arabic صديق means 'friend' — that is the NOUN sense of mate, not this verb definition at all; the upstream row appears to have taken the Arabic from the headword's other sense.

en_definition: something regarded with special favor or liking
note: Nominal sense is exactly what a learner meets ('this one is my favorite'). المفضل matches.

en_definition: a device in which something (usually an animal) can be caught and penned
note: The device-for-catching-animals sense is the one a learner meets. فخ matches exactly.

en_definition: the experiencing of affective and emotional states
note: The emotion sense is the right one. Wording is academic ('affective and emotional states') but a learner would still recognise the word; a plainer 'an emotion, or the state of experiencing one' would read better on a card. Arabic شُعُور is the standard compressed gloss for exactly this sense.

en_definition: cover from sight
expected: to put a dead body in the ground; to put something under ground or under a covering
note: 'cover from sight' is the broad WordNet umbrella (it licenses 'buried her face in her hands') and omits the defining element — putting into the ground. At rank 1135 the learner meets burial of the dead and buried treasure. Arabic دَفَنَ is the burial verb; it reads narrower than 'cover from sight' but Arabic دفن also extends to concealing, so I read it as faithful rather than divergent — and it happens to be closer to the sense the card should have had.

en_definition: (physics) a thermodynamic quantity equivalent to the capacity of a physical system to do work; the units of energy are joules or ergs
expected: the strength and liveliness you need to be active; also power from fuel or electricity
note: The physics gloss with joules and ergs is a technical sense displacing what a learner at rank 1141 meets — 'I have no energy today', 'renewable energy'. The parenthetical '(physics)' and the unit list make the card unusable for recognition. Arabic طاقة covers both readings and does not contradict the English; the defect is the English sense choice.

en_definition: have as a part, be made up out of
note: Correct commonest sense. Arabic تضمن matches.

en_definition: of comparatively great physical weight or density
note: Primary sense. Arabic ثقيل matches.

en_definition: a wide scarf worn about their shoulders by women
expected: past tense of 'steal' — took something that was not yours
note: Rank 1199 belongs almost entirely to the past tense of 'steal'; the garment is a real but marginal noun, and the ecclesiastical vestment rarer still. The POS tag 'noun' is how the wrong entry got selected — the frequency comes from a verb form the card never teaches. A learner drilling this will have learned a shawl and still not recognise 'he stole my bike'. The Arabic وشاح is a correct rendering of the definition as written, so this is an upstream sense-selection failure, not a translation one.

en_definition: refers back to a thing or animal already named ('the door closed ___ ')
note: Hand-written functional gloss with an example — good model for closed-class words. نَفْسُهُ is the right reflexive, carrying the masculine suffix that Arabic requires.

en_definition: the legal dissolution of a marriage
note: Commonest sense, correctly and compactly defined. طلاق is exact.

en_definition: a share set aside for a specific purpose
note: English sense is fine. Arabic تخصيص is the act of allocating, whereas the definition is the thing allocated ('a share set aside'); حصة مخصصة would match.

en_definition: a fund of money put by as a reserve
note: Commonest sense; مدخرات matches.

en_definition: express the need or desire for; ask for
note: Commonest sense. Minor form issue: طَلَب as vocalised reads most naturally as the noun 'a request'; for pos=verb the vocalisation طَلَبَ is the match.

en_definition: pose a threat to; present a danger to
expected: say you will harm or punish someone; also, put at risk
note: The endanger sense ('the flood threatens the town') is real and frequent, but the speech-act sense ('he threatened me', 'threatened to sue') is what a learner meets first at this rank. Close call — the two are near-tied. Arabic هدّد covers both and translates the definition faithfully.

en_definition: an inquiry into unfamiliar or questionable activities
note: Everyday sense, clean card. Arabic تحقيق is the standard equivalent; like most rows in this batch it is a one-word headword gloss rather than a rendering of the definition sentence, but it points at the same sense.

en_definition: situated in or facing or moving toward the east
note: Correct adjective sense (= eastern). Arabic شَرْق is the noun 'the east'; the adjective the definition describes is شَرْقِيّ. Same concept, wrong form for the tagged POS.

en_definition: in the direction of; the '-s' spelling ('walked ___ the door')
note: Hand-written gloss with a usage example, not a database sense — clean. Arabic نحو is the right preposition, though نحو also means 'approximately' and 'grammar/syntax' out of context.

en_definition: a licensed medical practitioner
note: Informal clipping of 'doctor' is the commonest sense; the definition's formal register ('a licensed medical practitioner') would equally define 'physician' and loses the colloquial marking — worth adding 'informal'. Some modern corpus hits are 'doc' = document/file, but the doctor sense still dominates speech. طبيب is correct though likewise unmarked for register.

en_definition: make whistling sounds
note: Sense is right for the verb (circular wording, but recognisable). Arabic صفّارة is the NOUN — the physical whistle you blow — not the verb 'to whistle', which is صفَر. Wrong part of speech, same family as the 'mate' error: the Arabic was taken from a different sense of the headword.

en_definition: like better; value more highly
note: Exactly right. Arabic فَضَّلَ matches.

en_definition: of or relating to China, its people or its culture; the language of China
note: Adjective sense is the everyday one; the appended 'the language of China' is a noun sense tacked on but both are common. صيني covers the adjective and the language alike.

en_definition: the act of orienting
expected: the direction something faces or is positioned in; also an introductory session for newcomers
note: Circular ('the act of orienting') and not the sense at this rank: everyday 'orientation' is a new-student/new-employee induction, a position or facing, or sexual orientation. The act-of-orienting reading is genuine but gives a learner nothing to recognise the word by. Arabic توجيه is a correct verbal-noun rendering of 'orienting/directing' and matches the definition as written.

en_definition: to say, state, or perform again
note: Commonest sense. كَرَّرَ matches.

en_definition: a relation between things or events (as in the case of one causing the other or sharing features with it)
note: The relation/link sense is the core one. Arabic عَلَاقَة matches it well.

en_definition: request urgently and forcefully
note: Commonest verb sense, well worded. Arabic طلب means plain 'request/ask for' and drops 'urgently and forcefully' — which is the entire thing separating demand from ask. Not a contradiction, but طالب بـ or طلب بإلحاح would carry the force.

en_definition: the extreme end of something; especially something pointed
note: The pointed-end sense is the core noun sense ('the tip of your finger', 'tip of the iceberg'). Two other common senses compete at this rank — a gratuity and a piece of advice — so if the card set allows multiple senses, those are worth adding rather than replacing this one. Arabic طَرَف is the end/extremity and matches the definition given.

en_definition: be able to spare or give up
expected: have enough money — or enough time — to be able to buy or do something
note: 'Be able to spare or give up' covers 'afford the time' but not the money sense that dominates at rank 1469 ('I can't afford a car'). Arabic أعطى = 'gave', which is the third, provide/yield sense of afford and not the English gloss given at all.

en_definition: occurring or encountered or experienced or observed frequently or in accordance with regular practice or procedure
note: Right sense, but the wording is a four-way 'or' chain lifted from a dictionary and is hard to read on a card; 'happening most of the time; normal or expected' carries the same sense. Arabic عادي is the correct everyday equivalent.

en_definition: a noisemaker (as at parties or games) that makes a loud noise when you blow through it
expected: a hard pointed growth on an animal's head; also the device in a car that sounds a warning
note: Classic displaced sense. At rank 1486 'horn' is an animal's horn or a car horn; the party blower is a marginal sense that has pushed both out. A learner would not recognise 'the bull's horns' or 'he honked his horn' from this card. The Arabic confirms the mismatch independently: قرن is the animal horn, which is not what the English definition describes at all (the car horn is بوق), so the English and Arabic sides of this card teach two different things.

en_definition: finely ground tobacco wrapped in paper; for smoking
note: Correct everyday sense; wording is fussy ("finely ground tobacco") but unambiguous. Arabic سِيجَارَة is the standard equivalent.

en_definition: carry out or perform an action
note: Sense is right (carry out, do). Card defect worth flagging separately: the definition contains the headword ('carry out or perform an action'), so it either gives the answer away or reads as circular. 'Carry out or complete an action or task' fixes it. Arabic أدّى is the correct rendering.

en_definition: a group of people living in a particular local area
note: Commonest everyday sense. Arabic مُجْتَمَع is a one-word gloss rather than a rendering of the whole phrase, but it points at the same sense and adds nothing the English lacks.

en_definition: a plot of ground where plants are cultivated
note: Primary sense, clearly worded. Arabic حديقة is the standard equivalent.

en_definition: the greatest possible degree of something
note: Broadly the core sense. 'Possible' is slightly off from everyday use, which is usually about what is permitted or set rather than what is achievable — speed limit, age limit, time limit — so 'the point or amount beyond which something may not go' would be a touch more accurate. Not a sense displacement. حدّ is the right word.

en_definition: lacking companions or companionship
note: Defensible as primary, but it describes the state of being alone rather than the feeling most speakers mean. Consider 'sad because you have no company or friends; also, isolated (a lonely road)'. Arabic وَحِيد matches 'lacking companions', though وَحِيد is also the everyday word for 'only/sole' (الابن الوحيد); يَشْعُر بِالوَحْدَة carries the affective sense.

en_definition: not clearly defined or easy to perceive or understand
note: Correct sense, plainly worded; غير واضح matches exactly. Aside: rank 1568 is implausibly high for this word and probably comes from subtitle corpora ('[indistinct chatter]') rather than real usage — a ranking artefact, not a definition problem.

en_definition: a timepiece that shows the time of day
note: Primary sense. Arabic ساعة matches; it also covers 'watch' and 'hour', which is normal Arabic polysemy rather than a translation error.

en_definition: an expression whose meaning cannot be determined from its context
expected: the quality of being unclear or open to more than one interpretation
note: Defines the countable instance (an ambiguous expression) rather than the abstract quality, which is what a learner meets at this rank. Arabic غموض is the quality sense (vagueness, obscurity), so it does not translate the definition as given — again the Arabic lands nearer the useful sense than the English does.

en_definition: have in mind as a purpose
note: English sense is the common one. Arabic تعمّد means 'did something deliberately/on purpose' — an action already done, often with a blaming connotation — not 'have in mind as a purpose'. Expected Arabic: نوى or قصد (or اعتزم for the planning sense).

en_definition: an enlarged and muscular saclike organ of the alimentary canal; the principal organ of digestion
note: The digestive organ is the sense a learner meets. Wording is anatomical ('alimentary canal', 'saclike') but unmistakable, and the second clause rescues it. Arabic معدة is exactly this organ.

en_definition: someone who has exceptional intellectual ability and originality
note: Commonest sense. Arabic عبقري matches 'someone who...' in both form and sense.

en_definition: any amazing or wonderful occurrence
expected: an extraordinary event that seems impossible and is believed to be caused by God or a supernatural power; also, loosely, an amazing piece of luck
note: 'Any amazing or wonderful occurrence' is the weakened everyday extension and strips out the supernatural element that distinguishes 'miracle' from 'wonder' or 'marvel'. The Arabic disagrees with the English as given: مُعْجِزَة is specifically a divine/prophetic miracle, not any amazing occurrence (that would be أعجوبة). Same shape of defect as 'board' — English gloss and Arabic gloss point at different senses.

en_definition: a dark region of considerable extent on the surface of the moon
expected: a woman's first name (the Spanish and Italian form of Mary)
note: This is a homograph collision, not a sense-ordering slip: the definition is for 'maria', the astronomical plural of 'mare' (the dark plains on the moon), while the word at rank 1679 is the given name María. The definition also describes one mare while the headword is plural. Nothing on this card helps a learner who hears the name in a film. If you prefer to treat the lunar term as the same lexical item, 'rare' is the fallback reading — either way the card is unusable. Arabic بحر قمري ('lunar sea') is a correct translation of the English as written, so the defect is entirely upstream.

en_definition: affected by an impairment of normal physical or mental function
note: Sick/unwell, correct. The gloss is stiff medical register for a rank-1698 adjective but the sense is right. مريض is exact.

en_definition: a series of things depending on each other as if linked together
expected: a row of metal rings linked together, used for pulling, fastening or securing
note: The figurative 'series of dependent things' (chain of events, chain of command) is real and common, but the physical linked-metal object is what an ordinary speaker means first. The Arabic سلسلة happens to span both the physical chain and the series, so it translates the given definition correctly.

en_definition: of or relating to or indicative of or issued or performed by a king or queen or other monarch
note: Right sense, though the chained 'of or relating to or indicative of or issued or performed by' is lexicographer prose a learner has to wade through. Arabic ملكي is exact.

en_definition: limbless scaly elongate reptile; some are venomous
note: English side is the obvious sense, well worded. The Arabic word choice is the weak point: حَنَش is dialectal/classical and in some usage covers lizards as well; the term a learner will actually meet is ثُعْبَان (or حَيَّة). Meaning is right, register is not — worth a translation-side fix even though I am not scoring it as a divergence.

en_definition: (Old Testament) the second wife of Jacob and mother of Joseph and Benjamin
expected: a woman's first name
note: At rank 1807 this is a given name heard in dialogue, not a biblical reference; the Old Testament figure is a genuine but narrow sense. The card at least establishes that Rachel is a woman's name, so it is less broken than a homograph collision, but a learner gains genealogy they will never use. Arabic راحيل is the correct name for that biblical figure and translates the definition as given.

en_definition: capital and largest city of Italy; on the Tiber; seat of the Roman Catholic Church; formerly the capital of the Roman Republic and the Roman Empire
note: Correct and unambiguous. Arabic is the name transliteration, consistent with the English, though like other proper nouns it conveys none of the descriptive detail.

en_definition: confess to a punishable or reprehensible deed, usually under pressure
note: Right sense, but the definition is circular — it contains the headword ('confess to a punishable... deed'), so on a recognition card it either gives the answer away or says nothing. Suggested rewrite: 'admit that you have done something wrong'. Arabic اعترف is exact.

en_definition: leisure time away from work devoted to rest or pleasure
note: Commonest sense. عُطْلَة matches. (The academic 'vacation' = university recess is the secondary sense and was correctly not chosen.)

en_definition: a surrounding or nearby region
expected: the area of a town where you live, and the people who live there
note: Classic displacement: the abstract "vicinity" sense ("in the neighborhood of $100") over the district-you-live-in sense a learner meets at this rank. Arabic جوار is a genuinely faithful translation of the definition as given — an upstream English problem, not a translation one. If the English is fixed, the Arabic must change to حيّ.

en_definition: leniency and compassion shown toward offenders by a person or agency charged with administering justice
expected: kindness or forgiveness shown to someone you could punish or harm
note: The judicial-clemency sense has displaced the general one. "Have mercy", "at the mercy of", "show mercy" are not about a person administering justice. Arabic رحمة is the broad mercy/compassion word and drops the restricting clause entirely — it lands on the everyday sense the English should have had, so English and Arabic are describing different things.

en_definition: a violent release of energy caused by a chemical or nuclear reaction
note: Correct core sense; اِنْفِجَار matches.

en_definition: get by special effort
expected: to make something safe or firmly fixed; also to obtain something with effort ('___ a loan')
note: 'Get by special effort' is a real and fairly common verb sense (secure funding, secure a deal), but the protect/make-safe sense is at least as likely for a learner and is what the adjective primes. A card carrying only the obtain sense will misfire on 'secure the building'. The Arabic يؤمّن means 'makes safe / insures' — it translates the OTHER sense, not the definition as given, so English and Arabic sides of this card teach two different words.

en_definition: (New Testament) the Apostle closely associated with St. Paul and traditionally assumed to be the author of the third Gospel
expected: a male given name; in the Bible, the author of the third Gospel
note: The evangelist is a real and recognised referent, but at rank 1980 'Luke' is overwhelmingly an ordinary male first name. Arabic لوقا is specifically the biblical Luke (the modern name would be لوك), so it tracks the definition given, correctly.

en_definition: referring to the first of two things or persons mentioned (or the earlier one or ones of several)
expected: from an earlier time; previous (a former president, her former husband)
note: The 'first of two mentioned' (the former ... the latter) sense is real but bookish; the everyday adjective means 'previous'. The Arabic سابق translates that everyday sense, NOT the contrastive definition on the card — the contrastive sense would need الأول (المذكور). Same shape as counsellor: the Arabic is right about the word and wrong about the definition, which points at the English.

en_definition: an undergraduate student during the year preceding graduation
expected: an older person; also a student in their final year of school or college
note: Real and common in US usage, but narrowed to undergraduates, which excludes the very common high-school sense and the elderly-person sense most speakers reach for with the bare noun. Arabic طالب السنة الأخيرة is an accurate compression of the definition as given.

en_definition: nonfictional prose forming an independent part of a publication
note: Right sense (the newspaper/magazine piece). Register is the problem, not the sense: 'nonfictional prose forming an independent part of a publication' is harder than the headword. 'A piece of writing in a newspaper, magazine or website' would carry the same sense at the learner's level. مقال is exact.

en_definition: endless loop of flexible material between two rotating shafts or pulleys
expected: a strip of leather or fabric worn around the waist
note: Textbook displacement: the drive/conveyor belt is real and reasonably common (fan belt, conveyor belt) but nobody thinks of it first at rank 2111 — the worn belt is the everyday sense. Note the Arabic disagrees with the English here: حِزَام is the waist belt; a belt running between pulleys is سَيْر in ordinary Arabic. So the gloss silently teaches the right sense while the English teaches the wrong one — fixing the English will also make the Arabic correct.

en_definition: not usual or common or ordinary
note: Exact, and the Arabic غير عادي mirrors it word for word.

en_definition: a nocturnal flying mammal with membranous wings; also to strike a ball with a club in cricket or baseball
expected: to hit a ball with a bat, as in cricket or baseball
note: POS conflation: the card is tagged verb but the definition leads with the noun (the animal) and appends the verb sense with 'also'. Both senses are common, but a verb card should give the verb. The Arabic خفاش renders only the animal half and is a noun, leaving the declared verb sense (ضرب الكرة) unrepresented — so an Arabic learner sees a noun gloss on a verb card.

en_definition: treat badly
note: English is fine: 'treat badly' is the commonest verb sense. The Arabic is wrong on two counts — مَسَبَّة is a NOUN meaning an insult or term of abuse, not the verb 'treat badly'. Expected يُسيء معاملة. A translation defect, not an upstream sense defect.

en_definition: English writer and lexicographer (1709-1784)
expected: a common English surname
note: Samuel Johnson (1709-1784) is a correct referent but a vanishingly uncommon one relative to the surname a learner actually meets at rank 2337; a proper noun of this kind is doubtful flashcard content at all. Arabic جونسون is the plain transliteration — says nothing false, but carries none of 'English writer and lexicographer'.

en_definition: restore by replacing a part or putting together what is torn or broken
note: Commonest sense (= fix). Note the archaic 'repair to a place' sense was correctly avoided. تَصْلِيح is the standard gloss, again a masdar for a verb entry.

en_definition: the time of person's life when they are a child
note: Correct and primary. Typo in the English string: "the time of person's life" is missing the article — should be "of a person's life". Arabic طفولة covers the definition exactly.

en_definition: an electrical phenomenon whereby an electromotive force (EMF) is generated in a closed circuit by a change in the flow of current
note: Technical, but this is the word's only sense — the word is specialist, the sense choice is not, so this is not a 'rare' hit. محاثة is the correct Arabic technical term. The real problem is rank 2415: 'inductance' is nowhere near 2,000th most frequent, so the frequency data for this row is suspect.

en_definition: a detailed description of design criteria for a piece of work
note: The 'spec document' sense, which is the ordinary one. Arabic مواصفات is plural for a singular headword; مُوَاصَفَة is the singular, though the plural is how the word is actually used.

en_definition: (mathematics) a mathematical relation such that each element of a given set (the domain of the function) is associated with an element of another set (the range of the function)
expected: the purpose or job that something or someone has; what a thing is used for
note: Classic sense-order failure: the mathematics sense displaces the everyday purpose/role sense a learner meets at rank 2502 ('the function of the heart', 'a phone with lots of functions'). The Arabic confirms the mismatch from the other direction — وَظِيفَة is job/role/purpose, not the mathematical object, which in Arabic is دالة. So the Arabic is right for the word and wrong for the definition as given.

en_definition: make reference to
note: 'Make reference to' is the commonest sense, though terse and slightly circular — 'to mention or talk about something' would be easier to recognise. Arabic أَشَارَ covers 'refer to / allude to' and matches.

en_definition: cry weakly or softly
note: Right sense, plainly put. Arabic يئن ('moans, groans softly') is a standard dictionary equivalent and carries 'cry weakly or softly' acceptably, though ينتحب بصوت خافت would be tighter.

en_definition: genre of art and literature and especially architecture in reaction against principles and practices of established modernism
note: Standard definition of the only sense. ما بعد الحداثة is the established Arabic term. Separate concern outside this audit: rank 2538 looks implausibly high for this word and may point at a frequency-list artefact.

en_definition: an artistic movement in Italy around 1910 that tried to express the energy and values of the machine age
expected: thinking about or trying to predict the future; also (capitalised) an early 20th-century Italian art movement celebrating machines and speed
note: The art movement is a legitimate and dictionary-first sense, but the live everyday sense is future-oriented forecasting (a futurist predicts trends). Also flag the rank: 2542 for 'futurism' looks like a corpus artifact rather than real frequency — worth checking upstream. مستقبلية does cover the art movement in Arabic as well as generic futurity, so it is compatible, though it conveys none of the 'Italy, around 1910' specifics.

en_definition: imagination unrestricted by reality
note: Sense is the common one (imagination / imagined things not real). Wording is abstract but recoverable. Arabic فنتازيا is a transliterated loanword that leans to the genre/spectacle sense and renders none of 'imagination unrestricted by reality'; خيال would translate the definition.

en_definition: lightly throw to see which side comes up
expected: to turn something over quickly, or flick it with a sudden movement
note: This is the coin-toss sense specifically. The everyday sense is 'turn over quickly' (flip a pancake, flip a switch, flip through a book); a learner would not recognise 'flip' from 'lightly throw to see which side comes up'. Note the Arabic قَلَبَ gives the general 'turn over/invert' sense — i.e. the Arabic is closer to the right sense than the English definition is, which is why it counts as diverging from the definition as written.

en_definition: of or relating to or resembling a bureaucrat or bureaucracy
note: Standard sense. The 'of or relating to or resembling' frame is WordNet boilerplate and reads stiffly, but the sense is the obvious one. بيروقراطي matches.

en_definition: the combined stakes of the betters
expected: a cat, especially a kitten (an affectionate or child's word)
note: The pooled-money sense is real and reasonably common ("put a fiver in the kitty"), but it is not what anyone meets first; the cat sense is. Telling detail: the Arabic هُرَيْرَة means 'kitten' — it translates the word's everyday sense, not the English definition shown, so English and Arabic on this card teach two different things.

en_definition: the state of being urgent; an earnest and insistent necessity
note: Plain and correct. Arabic إلحاح carries the insistent-pressing sense of the second clause well.

en_definition: any vehicle self-propelled by a rocket engine
note: Vehicle sense is the everyday one; the arugula/salad-plant sense was correctly avoided. صَارُوخ is exact (it covers both rocket and missile, as English 'rocket' loosely does).

en_definition: a cruel and brutal fellow
note: Right sense (the person who bullies), but the wording omits the defining element: picking on someone weaker, repeatedly. 'A cruel and brutal fellow' would equally yield brute, thug or tyrant, so recognition from this card is shaky. Arabic مُسْتَأْسِد ('one who lords it over others') carries domineering rather than 'cruel and brutal', a mild loosening but the same person.

en_definition: a label written or printed on paper, cardboard, or plastic that is attached to something to indicate its owner, nature, price, etc.
note: English is the correct primary sense (label). The Arabic زَقِيطَة is the problem: the standard term for a tag or label is بِطاقة (or لاصِقة). زقيطة is not recognisable Modern Standard Arabic in this meaning and reads as dialectal or corrupt. Flagged at moderate confidence — this one needs a native-speaker check rather than my judgement.

en_definition: an act of delaying or interrupting the continuity
note: Commonest sense; تعطيل matches.

en_definition: the capital and largest city of Japan; the economic and cultural center of Japan
note: Correct and the only sense. As with greece, Arabic طوكيو transliterates the headword rather than translating the definition, which gives the answer away on a recognition card.

en_definition: a thing constructed; a complex entity constructed of many parts
expected: the way the parts of something are arranged or organised; also a building or other thing that has been built
note: "A thing constructed" is the building sense; in ordinary use "structure" most often means arrangement or organisation (sentence structure, company structure). Not obscure, so a learner would still recognise it — just not the first sense they meet. هَيْكَل ('framework, skeleton, structure') fits the English as given.

en_definition: as the agent of or on someone's part (usually expressed as  rather than )
expected: in the interest of, or as the representative of, someone (normally used as 'on behalf of')
note: SENSE IS CORRECT — the expected text here is a string repair, not a sense change. The card's parenthetical has had its quoted examples stripped: it renders as 'usually expressed as  rather than ', two empty slots where WordNet has 'on behalf of' rather than 'in behalf of'. That is an upstream text-extraction bug (quoted material dropped) and will read as broken to a learner; worth grepping the corpus for other glosses containing 'expressed as' or double spaces inside parentheses. نيابة عن is the right rendering.

en_definition: persistent determination
note: Only sense in ordinary use; مثابرة is the exact equivalent.

en_definition: after death the soul begins a new cycle of existence in another human body
expected: a fresh start or revival; new life or growth after a decline
note: This is the reincarnation sense. Real and recognisable in religious contexts, but everyday "rebirth" is renewal/revival (the rebirth of a city, a spiritual rebirth). Arabic تناسخ الأرواح translates the English as given, correctly — the defect is upstream, in the sense chosen.

en_definition: recite with musical intonation; recite as a chant or a psalm
note: English gives the right verb sense, though it is partly circular ('recite as a chant'). Arabic أهزوجة is a NOUN ('a chant, a cheer') under a verb entry and renders none of 'recite with musical intonation'; يُنشد or يُرتّل is what the definition says.

en_definition: come into rough contact with while moving
expected: push someone or something roughly and with force
note: 'Come into rough contact with while moving' is the jostle sense — real ('he shoved past me') but not the first one anybody thinks of, which is a hard deliberate push. The definition is also passive-sounding where the word is forceful and intentional. Telling detail: the Arabic يدفع بعنف ('pushes violently') translates the sense the card should have used, not the sense it gives — so the Arabic is better than the English here, and diverges from it.

en_definition: the trait of staying aware of (paying close attention to) your responsibilities
expected: the practice of paying calm, focused attention to the present moment
note: The WordNet sense — heedfulness of one's responsibilities, i.e. conscientiousness — is why this word is in the frequency list at all only in older text. In contemporary English at rank 2989 'mindfulness' means the meditation/wellbeing practice almost every time; a learner meeting this card would not recognise the word in the wild. Arabic يقظة ('alertness, wakefulness') drops the load-bearing 'your responsibilities' part and points at the present-moment-awareness sense instead (يَقَظَة ذِهْنِيَّة is the standard Arabic term for the meditation sense), so it does not render the definition as given.

en_definition: a state in the eastern United States; one of the original 13 colonies; one of the Confederate States in the American Civil War
note: Correct identification of the US state. Separate issue, outside this rubric: a lowercase proper noun as a vocabulary card is questionable value at rank 3019. The Arabic is a transliteration of the name rather than a translation of the descriptive sentence — it says nothing the English does not, so faithful, but it carries none of the 'eastern US / original 13 colonies' content.

en_definition: immunity from arbitrary exercise of authority: political independence
expected: freedom to act or think as you choose, without control by others
note: The political-philosophy sense is real and central to this word, but 'immunity from arbitrary exercise of authority' is abstract enough that a learner will not map it to 'freedom'. The colon-joined double gloss ('...authority: political independence') also reads as two definitions on one card. Arabic حرية is the right word and covers both readings.

en_definition: spring back; spring away from an impact
note: Ball-rebound sense, exactly right. يرتد matches 'spring back'.

en_definition: any physical damage to the body caused by violence or accident or fracture etc.
expected: a deeply distressing experience, and the lasting emotional harm it leaves
note: The physical-injury sense is real and current in medicine, but at rank 3274 the sense a learner meets is psychological ('childhood trauma'). Arabic إصابة ('injury') translates the English definition as given correctly — this is an upstream sense-choice problem, not a translation one.

en_definition: impossible or nearly impossible to see; imperceptible by the eye
note: Primary sense. Arabic غير مرئي is the exact equivalent.

en_definition: tavern consisting of a building with a bar and public rooms; often provides light meals
note: Correct, if wordy. Arabic حَانَة matches 'tavern'.

en_definition: inquire into
expected: travel through an unfamiliar place to find out what it is like; also examine an idea or option carefully
note: 'Inquire into' captures the figurative sense ('explore the options') and is genuinely common, but the first image for an ordinary speaker is physical — exploring a cave, a city, a continent. Two words is also thin for a rank-3293 card. Arabic اِسْتَكْشَفَ spans both senses and leans toward the physical one, so it covers 'inquire into' loosely rather than precisely; low confidence on this faithfulness call.

en_definition: promise solemnly; also a solemn pledge to do something or behave in a certain way
note: Correct everyday sense with both verb and noun covered. Arabic نَذَرَ is a standard dictionary equivalent but skews religious (a vow made to God, also 'to consecrate'); تعهّد or أقسم would render 'promise solemnly' more neutrally. Not a divergence, but worth a note if the gloss pass revisits it.

en_definition: bend or lay so that one part covers the other
note: The obvious everyday sense, plainly worded. طَوَى is the standard verb and matches.

en_definition: a member of the extinct Algonquian people formerly living in northern Indiana and southern Michigan
expected: a large city on the coast of southern Florida
note: At rank 3360 this is the Florida city in essentially every occurrence; the Algonquian people is a real but obscure sense. The definition also calls the people 'extinct', which is inaccurate — the Miami Tribe of Oklahoma exists. Arabic مياميّون faithfully renders the ethnonym sense the English gives.

en_definition: United States actor (1914-1998)
expected: a variant spelling of marshal — an officer of high rank, or someone who organises an event; also a common surname
note: "United States actor (1914-1998)" is an encyclopaedia entry for one person (E.G. Marshall), not a definition of a word — nothing is learnable from it. The rank comes from the surname and from Marshall Plan / marshal. Arabic مارشال is a transliteration of the name, which is the only sensible rendering of a person entry, so the defect is entirely in the English.

en_definition: a joint between the distal end of the radius and the proximal row of carpal bones
note: Sense is correct — this is the only sense — but the register is medical anatomy ('distal end of the radius', 'proximal row of carpal bones') and a learner cannot parse it. Recommend rewording to 'the joint between the hand and the arm'. Not a sense defect, a register defect. مِعْصَم names the same joint.

en_definition: a sweetheart chosen to receive a greeting on Saint Valentine's Day
expected: a card or message sent on Saint Valentine's Day; also the person you send it to
note: The sweetheart sense is real ("be my valentine"), but the card sense is at least as common and is the one most learners meet first. Arabic حبيب ('beloved') renders the English as given, just less specifically — it loses the Saint Valentine's Day tie.

en_definition: a hand-held mobile radiotelephone for use in an area divided into small sections, each with its own short-range transmitter/receiver
note: Right sense, but the wording is an engineering spec: 'radiotelephone', 'an area divided into small sections', 'short-range transmitter/receiver'. It explains why cellular networks are called cellular, which no learner asked. 'A mobile phone you carry with you' is the whole content. Arabic هاتف محمول is the plain everyday term and drops the network detail — a sensible simplification rather than a divergence.

en_definition: accomplishment of an objective
expected: the act of arriving at a place; coming
note: Clear case of the lexical database's abstract sense ('arrival at a conclusion') displacing the obvious one. Nobody meeting 'arrival' at rank 3623 means accomplishment of an objective — they mean arrivals at the airport. Arabic وصول carries 'arrival/reaching/attainment', so it is not a mistranslation, but it does not render 'of an objective' and reads as the plain arrival sense the English failed to give.

en_definition: United States general in the Union Army who was defeated at Chancellorsville by Robert E. Lee (1814-1879)
expected: informal: a prostitute
note: Textbook proper-noun displacement: the card defines Joseph Hooker, a Union general, where the word a learner meets at rank 3678 means a prostitute (or, in rugby, the front-row forward who hooks the ball). A learner cannot recover the headword from this and would learn nothing usable. Worth considering whether the word belongs on a card at all given the register.

en_definition: a container; usually has a lid
expected: a container for rubbish, or for storing things
note: The superordinate gloss ("a container; usually has a lid") is not wrong but is too generic to identify the word — it fits box, tub, chest or canister equally — and omits the rubbish sense that dominates everyday use. The Arabic is a separate and worse defect: مزبلة is a rubbish dump or dunghill, a place, with a pejorative edge, not a lidded container. Should be سلة المهملات or حاوية.

en_definition: give an education to
note: Slightly circular but unmistakable. Arabic يُعَلم matches.

en_definition: susceptible to attack
expected: easily harmed or hurt, physically or emotionally; open to attack or damage
note: Same broad sense, but 'susceptible to attack' narrows it to military/security contexts and will not help with the commonest modern uses — 'vulnerable children', 'vulnerable to criticism', 'felt vulnerable'. Arabic عرضة ('exposed, liable to') tracks the definition, though as a citation form it is an incomplete collocation (عرضة للهجوم).

en_definition: drop a hint; intimate by a hint
note: Sense is right (to suggest something indirectly) but the definition is circular — it uses 'hint' twice, so the card explains the headword with the headword and teaches nothing. Suggested rewrite: 'to suggest something indirectly instead of saying it outright'. The Arabic تَلْمِيح is the NOUN (a hint, an allusion) while this entry is the verb and the definition is a verb phrase; the verb would be يُلَمِّح / يُلْمِح.

en_definition: conceal or hide
expected: make a sound quieter or less clear, especially by covering it
note: 'Conceal or hide' is an abstracted wrapping sense; nobody reaches for 'muffle' to mean 'hide', and a learner shown this card would never recover the word or the sound sense they will actually meet ('a muffled scream').
